questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors, you should practice using them because:

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It can be hard to remember to check mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road behind you. However, they make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice using your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When being passed by another vehicle, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your risk of a collision. Riding on the far side is also unsafe because it may tempt the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The group will pull off at the next exit.

questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points their index finger up, it means the group should move into a single-file line.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Maintain proper distance from other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain proper distance from other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and check your mirrors often. Both the lead and back riders should be experienced. Keep safe space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: The clothing you wear while riding should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Riding clothing should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, cold, dehydration, and injuries from the motorcycle. It also gives extra protection in case of a crash.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: Will be similar to a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Adding weight to your motorcycle increases stopping distance. Start slowing down and braking earlier when carrying a load or passenger in the sidecar.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Use headlights from vehicles ahead to see better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use headlights from vehicles ahead to see better.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase following distance when riding at night. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be ready to change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with sidecar handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. The best path through a curve may move from the outside to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: How should a rider sit to best control a motorcycle?

options.text: Using arms to hold the body up.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should bend slightly at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: When are motorcycle helmets required?

options.text: For riders under 21 or those with a license for less than one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: For riders under 21 or those with a license for less than one year.
questions.explanation: In Rhode Island, riders under 21 or those with a license for less than one year must wear a helmet. Helmets are recommended for all riders.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
Lean in the direction you want to go when turning.
Avoid dragging your feet on the road.

questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet, as they could catch and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you from injury in a crash and shields you from weather problems like hot or cold conditions.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position increases your visibility and helps you avoid blind spots, wind blasts, and hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.explanation: Before carrying a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This prevents them from falling behind and allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: If road conditions need more stopping distance, what should you do?

options.text: Let someone else ride your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: When your motorcycle needs more distance to stop, increase your following distance. Use at least a three-second gap if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with red lights flashing?

options.text: You must slow down and be careful.
You do not need to slow down.

questions.explanation: When you see a stopped school bus with red lights flashing, you must stop completely until the lights stop flashing. The only exception is if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When do you not need a large following distance?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.
When you cannot see past the vehicle ahead.
When the weather is good and traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the weather is good and traffic is light.
questions.explanation: You need extra following distance in bad conditions. Increase your distance if the road is wet, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy. You need less distance only in good weather and light traffic.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps drivers see you best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding to be more visible. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: How should you position your motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: Stay in one lane position at all times.
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane so drivers see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move around the lane based on what road and traffic conditions require at that moment.

questions.question: What is the best way to brake straight and hard?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking the wheels.
Use both brakes at the same time and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: The best straight braking uses both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Do not lock either wheel.
